lines.trans: Did a heavy truck just drive down Jasmine Street, Tariq?
No trucks at midnight. Look through the lobby glass—lightning!
Oh no! You took all four wooden shutters off their hinges after sanding them!
And they are leaning bare against the courtyard wall right now!
If bare dry wood gets soaked tonight, Monday's green paint will never stick!
Grab the back door lantern, Nour—first big drops are already falling!
I have the left end of shutter one—lift and run for the hallway!
Good! Two down, two more outside—watch the wet stones!
Got the last pair just as the sky opened up! Whew, my sleeves are soaked!
The wood is bone-dry, Nour. You move fast in a storm.
Wait—if it pours all day Monday, where do we paint four tall shutters?!

Did a heavy truck just drive down Jasmine Street, Tariq?
No trucks at midnight. Look through the lobby glass—lightning!
Oh no! You took all four wooden shutters off their hinges after sanding them!
And they are leaning bare against the courtyard wall right now!

Grab the back door lantern, Nour—first big drops are already falling!
I have the left end of shutter one—lift and run for the hallway!
Good! Two down, two more outside—watch the wet stones!
Got the last pair just as the sky opened up! Whew, my sleeves are soaked!
The wood is bone-dry, Nour. You move fast in a storm.
Wait—if it pours all day Monday, where do we paint four tall shutters?!

Did a heavy truck just drive down Jasmine Street, Tariq?
No trucks at midnight. Look through the lobby glass—lightning!

Grab the back door lantern, Nour—first big drops are already falling!

lines.trans: Look at our Monday forecast... heavy rain until Tuesday noon!
Until next time!

meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Second person masculine singular pronoun.

examples.trans: Did you plant these herbs yourself?
Did you plan this entire meeting?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one woman.

examples.trans: You must be Nour!
You are today's heroine, Nour.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: He called us on Tuesday.
The corner shop is open every Tuesday.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of الاثنين ('Monday', and with ال also 'both / the two').

examples.trans: I started work on Monday morning.
Monday's bus arrived at seven.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

meanings.note: The n-pattern of فتح: the thing opens by itself, nobody is named (الباب انفتح 'the door came open').

examples.trans: The window blew open by itself in the wind.
The old lock does not open easily.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Flash of lightning in a storm, often paired with رعد ('thunder').

examples.text: شفنا برق قوي ورا قزاز الباب.
examples.trans: We saw bright lightning behind the door glass.

examples.text: بعد البرق بثواني، سمعنا صوت الرعد.
examples.trans: Seconds after the lightning, we heard the roll of thunder.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببلش, بيبلش).

examples.trans: The brass pipe started heating up right away!
The clock tower started chiming twelve.

meanings.note: Form V intransitive verb meaning 'get wet / soaked in the rain'.

examples.text: دخلنا الشيش جوا قبل ما يتبلل الخشب.
examples.trans: We brought the shutters inside before the wood got soaked.
My sleeves got a little wet from the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Opposite of أمامي ('front').

examples.text: الفانوس معلق جنب الباب الخلفي للساحة.
examples.trans: The lantern hangs beside the back door to the courtyard.

examples.text: الغرفة الخلفية أهدى غرفة بالبيت كله.
examples.trans: The back room is the quietest room in the whole house.

meanings.note: Form II causative of دخل ('enter'), meaning 'carry/bring indoors'.

examples.text: دخلنا الكراسي الخشب للممر قبل المطر.
examples.trans: We brought the wooden chairs into the hallway before the rain.
Help me carry the baskets into the kitchen.

meanings.note: Single hinged panel or leaf of a double window, shutter, or cupboard.

examples.text: فتحنا الدرفة الشمال وبعدين الدرفة اليمين.
examples.trans: We swung open the left shutter leaf and then the right one.

examples.text: كل شباك إله درفتين خشب متينات.
examples.trans: Each window has two sturdy wooden shutter panels.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

meanings.note: Standard verb for lifting something up or raising.

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بركض, بيركض).

examples.text: اركضي بسرعة قبل ما يصحوا الضيوف!
examples.trans: Run fast before the guests wake up!
You ran across half the town this morning.

meanings.note: Used in the mild exclamation يا ساتر! ('goodness! / heaven forbid!').

examples.trans: Goodness, I nearly dropped the glass!
Goodness, what heavy rain outside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سريعة, plural: سريعين).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
Quick service and a kind smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سماوات.

examples.trans: The evening sky is clear and calm.
The lanterns are glowing beneath the sky.

meanings.note: Heavy delivery truck or freight lorry.

examples.text: فكرنا صوت الرعد شاحنة كبيرة مارة بالشارع.
examples.trans: We thought the rumble of thunder was a big truck passing down the street.

examples.text: الشاحنات الكبيرة ما بتدخل الحارة بالليل.
examples.trans: Heavy trucks do not drive into the neighbourhood at night.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Levantine word for slatted window shutters, used as a collective: الشيش مسكر 'the shutters are closed'.

examples.trans: Close the shutters, the sun is strong.
Green shutters suit the house.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Woodworker's word for sanding timber smooth; ورق صنفرة is sandpaper.

examples.text: خلصنا صنفرة الدرفات الأربعة قبل المغرب.
examples.trans: We finished sanding all four shutter panels before sunset.

examples.text: اشتريت ورق صنفرة ناعم للخشب القديم.
examples.trans: I bought fine-grit sandpaper for the old wood.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation (duhur) for midday (12:00 p.m.).

examples.text: الكافيه بيقدم شوربة سخنة من الضهر للمسا.
examples.trans: The café serves hot soup from noon until evening.

examples.text: الشمس بتكون عالية ودافية وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The sun is high and warm at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أطراف.

examples.trans: Pull the edge of the sheet tight.

examples.text: حط الكاسة بعيد عن طرف الطاولة.
examples.trans: Set the glass away from the edge of the table.

meanings.note: Form II طلّع means both 'look!' (طلّع بالمراية) and 'bring/carry up' (رح أطلّع الشنتة).

examples.text: طلع بالمراية ورا المكتب يا معلم!
examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk, boss!
I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Can refer to physical length, height, or duration of time (e.g., all day).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Used to describe a tall person or a long object.

examples.text: في رجال طويل واقف عند البوابة.
examples.trans: There is a tall man standing by the gate.
Three years was a long time.

meanings.note: Strong wind-and-rain storm.

examples.text: دخلنا كل إشي جوا قبل ما تبلش العاصفة.
examples.trans: We brought everything indoors before the storm hit.

examples.text: هديت العاصفة الصبح وطلعت الشمس عالحجار.
examples.trans: The storm calmed in the morning and sunlight hit the stones.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Standard collocation with rain: مطر غزير ('heavy downpour').

examples.text: نزل مطر غزير طول الليل وغسل الشجر.
examples.trans: Heavy rain fell all night and washed the trees clean.

examples.text: النشرة بتتوقع مطر غزير لبكرا الضهر.
examples.trans: The forecast predicts heavy rain until tomorrow noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Geminate verb for unscrewing hinges, bolts, or panels.

examples.text: طارق فك اللوح الأمامي للبيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: Tariq unscrewed the front panel of the piano gently.
We took the shutter panels off to sand them in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

كب.gloss: to spill; pour out; pour down (rain)

meanings.en: to spill; pour out; pour down (rain)
meanings.note: Quintessential Jordanian verb for spilling coffee, throwing out water, or rain pouring down (عم تكب مطر).

examples.text: امسك الفنجان منيح قبل ما تكب القهوة.
examples.trans: Hold the cup steady before you spill the coffee.

examples.text: السما بلشت تكب مطر بنص الليل.
examples.trans: The sky started pouring rain at midnight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Vocalized lemma distinguishing 'sleeve' (kumm, pl. kmaam كمام) from كم ('how many?').

examples.text: شمرت عن كمامي قبل ما نغسل الشبابيك.
examples.trans: I rolled up my sleeves before we washed the windows.

examples.text: تبللت كمام قميصي لما ركضنا تحت المطر.
examples.trans: My shirt sleeves got soaked when we ran in the rain.

meanings.note: Used to mark the limit of a time period, distance, or extent in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: We waited until you called us.
I stayed up until midnight.

meanings.note: Intransitive/transitive verb meaning 'stick fast' (paint on dry wood, stamp on postcard).

examples.text: الدهان ما بيلزق منيح عالخشب المبلول.
examples.trans: Paint does not stick well to wet wood.

examples.text: لزقنا ورقة المواعيد على باب المطبخ.
examples.trans: We stuck the schedule sheet onto the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليالي.

examples.trans: The guest arrived last night.
The neighbourhood is very quiet at night.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مبلولة, plural: مبلولين).

examples.trans: The wet wood on the shutters softens the echo.
His coat was wet from the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مداخل.

examples.trans: The guesthouse entrance is lit by a brass lantern.
We greeted the guests at the entrance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمر, بيمر).

examples.trans: Pass right beside the green pharmacy.

examples.text: أنا مريت من جنب السبيل الحجري!
examples.trans: I just passed the stone fountain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسك, بيمسك).

examples.trans: Hold this torch steady right here.
Grab the boxes, Tariq!

meanings.note: Passive participle describing panels, ladders, or chairs leaning against a wall.

examples.text: السلم الخشب مسند على حيط الساحة.
examples.trans: The wooden ladder is leaning against the courtyard wall.

examples.text: درفات الشيش كانت مسندة برا بعد الصنفرة.
examples.trans: The shutter panels were propped outside after sanding.

meanings.note: Standard word for rain, commonly used across all registers of Arabic.

examples.trans: Please come inside out of the cold rain.
The trees are green and lovely after the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مفصلات.

examples.text: حطيت نقطة زيت على مفصلة الباب.
examples.trans: I put a drop of oil on the door hinge.
The brass hinges of the chest are intact.

meanings.note: Describes sanded bare wood (خشب مكشوف) or an open-air courtyard.

examples.text: الخشب المكشوف بعد الصنفرة لازم يضل ناشف.
examples.trans: Bare wood after sanding has to stay dry.
We sat in the open courtyard beneath the stars.

meanings.note: Very common word of approval or rating something highly.

examples.trans: The reading light beside the desk is excellent.
The shower water was hot and excellent!

meanings.note: An inside hallway or a narrow passage between buildings.

examples.trans: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
The hallway is dark, turn on the light.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Can refer to objects lacking moisture or metaphorically to a rude or blunt person.

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat.
The attic is dry and warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Short for نشرة الطقس / النشرة الجوية ('weather forecast').

examples.text: نشرة يوم التنين بتقول في مطر غزير الصبح.
examples.trans: Monday's forecast says heavy rain in the morning.

examples.text: خليني أشوف نشرة الطقس قبل ما ندهن برا.
examples.trans: Let me check the weather forecast before we paint outside.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Can refer to a physical dot, a score point, or a drop of liquid.

examples.trans: Not a single drop of juice got on the table!

examples.text: شرب كل نقطة من الشوربة السخنة.
examples.trans: He drank every drop of the hot soup.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: General term for time or duration.

examples.trans: Old pipes take time to warm up.
You arrived right on time.

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
